name: Modest Mouse
label: Matador
lede: A kid from a trailer in Issaquah, a bassist he met at a video store and a drummer found at a metal show made the Northwest's most restless records, then got a Smith, a platinum hit and three decades of trouble to go with them.

eras.title: Issaquah, on purpose
eras.text: Modest Mouse came together in Issaquah, Washington, a suburb east of Seattle, and Isaac Brock kept it there on purpose: not Seattle, not Olympia, just strip malls and cul-de-sacs to write about. The first records went through Calvin Johnson's orbit in Olympia and then to Up Records.

years.h: Isaac Brock, Eric Judy and Jeremiah Green start Modest Mouse
years.p: Isaac Brock met bassist Eric Judy at a video store outside Seattle when both were teenagers, and the pair found drummer Jeremiah Green at a heavy metal show.
years.xp:
Brock was born in Helena, Montana, and moved to Issaquah at 11. According to Wikipedia he was raised in Grace Gospel Church and was asked to speak in tongues at age six. Religion runs all through his songs.

The band name comes from a line in Virginia Woolf's short story The Mark on the Wall about modest, mouse-coloured people. It has nothing to do with the composer Modest Mussorgsky, whatever the jokes say.

years.h: Blue Cadet-3, Do You Connect? EP · K Records
years.p: Modest Mouse cuts its first EP at Calvin Johnson's Dub Narcotic Studio in Olympia, with John Wickhart on bass and Dann Gallucci on guitar.

years.h: Sad Sappy Sucker is recorded, then shelved for seven years
years.p: Modest Mouse's first album for K Records, Sad Sappy Sucker, is recorded in 1994, hit by delay after delay, and forgotten. K finally releases it in 2001.

years.h: This Is a Long Drive..., the debut LP on Up Records
years.p: Steve Wold, later famous as the bluesman [[Seasick Steve|231ff972-4e8e-4157-95e2-12f963cb478c]], records Modest Mouse's first full-length at Moon Studios in Olympia. The Interstate 8 EP follows the same year.
play: This Is a Long Drive for Someone with Nothing to Think About

eras.title: The greatest Northwest record ever made
eras.text: The Lonesome Crowded West turned a cult band into a cause: a sprawling, furious record about highways, malls and bad religion that sold steadily without a hit. It also brought the majors calling.

q: The Lonesome Crowded West is the greatest Northwest record ever made.
years.h: The Lonesome Crowded West · Up Records
years.p: Recorded between May 22 and June 7, 1997, at Moon Studios in Olympia with Calvin Johnson and Scott Swayze. Pitchfork gave it 8.9, then upgraded it to 10 in 2014.
years.xp:
Phil Ek recorded three tracks in Seattle. By June 2000, according to Nielsen SoundScan figures cited on Wikipedia, it had sold over 60,000 copies in the US, all without a radio single.

In 2014 Brock's own label, Glacial Pace, put it back on vinyl in its original two-cover package.

years.h: Modest Mouse keeps playing Speak in Tongues in Cleveland
years.p: Long after Modest Mouse could fill bigger rooms, the band kept booking DIY punk spaces like Speak in Tongues in Cleveland, Ohio.

years.h: Isaac Brock's jaw is broken mid-album in Chicago
years.p: During five months at Clava Studios in Chicago for The Moon & Antarctica, Isaac Brock was attacked near the band's lodging. His jaw was broken and wired shut.
years.xp:
Producer [[Brian Deck|e91d5dc5-12a7-45cf-af2b-f120def0f711]] of [[Califone|68025033-de1b-42f5-8a21-bedfb8895dda]] says Brock spent a week in hospital and had his jaw wired for two or three months. The studio wasn't even finished when the band arrived.

Deck and Brock had met on a shared bill at the Magic Stick in Detroit, where they hung out until the end of the night.

eras.title: Epic, a minivan and a breakdown
eras.text: The first major-label record was bleaker and stranger than anything before it, and critics adored it. Then came a car commercial, a festival package tour and, in 2003, the loss of the founding drummer.

years.h: The Moon & Antarctica · Epic Records
years.p: Modest Mouse's major-label debut gets a 9.8 from Pitchfork, the site's third-best album of 2000. Up Records puts out the rarities set Building Nothing Out of Something the same year.

years.big: A minivan ad, and no apology
q: can bitch about my principles while they spend their parents' money
years.h: Modest Mouse sells Gravity Rides Everything to Nissan
years.p: Modest Mouse licenses Gravity Rides Everything from The Moon & Antarctica to a Nissan Quest commercial. Isaac Brock calls it commercial, and necessary.
years.xp: Brock didn't pretend otherwise. He said the money kept the band alive and aimed his answer at fans with trust funds and dish-washing jobs.

years.h: Modest Mouse joins the Unlimited Sunshine Tour
years.p: A package bill with [[Cake|fa7b9055-3703-473a-8a09-adf2fe031a24]], [[De La Soul|a8ebde98-7e91-46c7-992c-90039ba42017]], [[The Flaming Lips|1f43d76f-8edf-44f6-aaf1-b65f05ad9402]], the Hackensaw Boys and Kinky. Isaac Brock also releases Sharpen Your Teeth as [[Ugly Casanova|5c2d7596-2366-47c5-b4a2-0550ac8f9e69]].

years.h: Jeremiah Green quits Modest Mouse on his 26th birthday
years.p: Jeremiah Green leaves after a breakdown; the official line said he was going to his side band Vells. [[Helio Sequence|b6ab8d01-0cb3-4515-bc05-d928397e7429]] drummer Benjamin Weikel and returning guitarist Dann Gallucci step in.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, Green had been hospitalized, was diagnosed with bipolar disorder, and had severe manic episodes when medication was mixed with alcohol and mushrooms. He came back briefly, then disappeared for two months during recording sessions in Portland.

eras.title: Float On, everywhere
eras.text: The record made without Green became the one everybody knew. A public radio show, late-night TV and two Grammy nominations turned a band that once played Cleveland basements into a platinum act.

years.h: Good News for People Who Love Bad News goes platinum
years.p: Float On and Ocean Breathes Salty become hits, the album is later certified platinum, and public radio's Marketplace uses Float On as bumper music.
play: Good News for People Who Love Bad News

years.h: Jeremiah Green rejoins Modest Mouse
years.p: Jeremiah Green is back behind the kit a month after Good News comes out. Benjamin Weikel goes back to [[Helio Sequence|b6ab8d01-0cb3-4515-bc05-d928397e7429]] full time.

years.h: Isaac Brock's adopted brother dies on Mount Rainier
years.p: Isaac Brock's adopted brother, Ansel Vizcaya, is killed in an avalanche on Mount Rainier.

years.h: Isaac Brock signs Wolf Parade to Sub Pop
years.p: Working on Sub Pop's A&R team, Isaac Brock signs Montreal's [[Wolf Parade|b7ddce8b-9e5c-46bd-9d33-41b134ce1a7f]].

years.h: Modest Mouse plays Float On on Saturday Night Live
years.p: Modest Mouse plays Float On and Ocean Breathes Salty on SNL. Good News gets Grammy nominations for Best Alternative Album and, for Float On, Best Rock Song.

eras.title: A Smith joins the band
eras.text: Johnny Marr of The Smiths signed on as a full member, and the band's next record went straight to No. 1. Then Marr left, and in 2012 so did Eric Judy, the last founder beside Brock and Green.

years.h: Johnny Marr of The Smiths joins Modest Mouse
years.p: Dann Gallucci quits amicably and Johnny Marr takes his place as a full member, not a hired gun.

years.h: Modest Mouse is cut off early at Florida's Bang festival
years.p: Modest Mouse's set at the Bang Music Festival is cut short. The band doesn't play Miami, Orlando or St. Augustine again until June 2008.

years.h: We Were Dead Before the Ship Even Sank hits No. 1
years.p: Delayed from December 2006, it becomes Modest Mouse's first No. 1 on the Billboard 200, with Dashboard, Missed the Boat and We've Got Everything as singles.
play: We Were Dead Before the Ship Even Sank

years.h: Heath Ledger's King Rat video is left unfinished
years.p: Heath Ledger loved Modest Mouse's King Rat before its release and began a video with his collective The Masses. He died in January 2008 before finishing it.

years.h: Johnny Marr leaves Modest Mouse for The Cribs
years.p: Johnny Marr joins [[The Cribs|a3a92047-be1c-4f3e-8960-c4f8570984df]] and Jim Fairchild takes the guitar spot. No One's First, and You're Next, an EP of leftovers, follows on August 4.

years.h: Founding bassist Eric Judy leaves Modest Mouse
years.p: Eric Judy departs after nearly two decades; Russell Higbee of [[Man Man|4e210d41-b3e3-4e34-8c3b-3b8cc2116562]] takes bass. Pitchfork.tv also airs a 45-minute film on The Lonesome Crowded West.

eras.title: Glacial pace
eras.text: Eight years passed between albums. Brock took back his old records on his own label, Glacial Pace, and the band came back bigger, with violins and extra percussion.

years.h: Glacial Pace reissues the first two Modest Mouse albums
years.p: Isaac Brock's label puts This Is a Long Drive... and The Lonesome Crowded West back out on CD and vinyl.

years.h: Strangers to Ourselves ends an eight-year wait
years.p: Modest Mouse's first album since 2007, preceded by Lampshades on Fire, which debuted on Minnesota public station 89.3 The Current.

years.h: A study ranks Modest Mouse indie rock's second-most profane
years.p: A Musixmatch analysis of 43,414 songs puts Modest Mouse behind only The Neighbourhood, with a swear word every 310 words.

years.h: The Golden Casket, the last album with Jeremiah Green
years.p: Modest Mouse's seventh album. The Wall Street Journal called its first half overstuffed and praised the stripped-down closer Back to the Middle.

eras.title: Losing Jeremiah
eras.text: A 25th-anniversary tour for The Lonesome Crowded West ended with the death of the drummer who played on it. Brock kept going: the 2004 line-up for a victory lap, then an eighth album with new players.

years.h: Jeremiah Green dies of cancer at 45
years.p: Jeremiah Green took unannounced leave from the Lonesome Crowded West 25th-anniversary tour. His stage IV cancer was made public on December 25; he died in Sequim, Washington, six days later.
years.xp: Green played on every Modest Mouse album but one, from the first EP to The Golden Casket. Stylus Magazine had ranked him 37th among the greatest rock drummers.

years.h: Isaac Brock revives the Good News line-up for a tour
years.p: Benjamin Weikel returns to celebrate Good News for People Who Love Bad News. Eric Judy, Dann Gallucci and Tom Peloso do not. That summer Modest Mouse co-headlines with [[Pixies|b6b2bb8d-54a9-491f-9607-7b546023b433]].

years.h: An Eraser and a Maze, the eighth album
years.p: Modest Mouse's first album in five years, with new members Simon O'Connor, Damon Cox and Keith Karman. Brock says a Golden Casket companion, Shadows in the Shade, is due around 2027.
years.xp: Brock told Paste that Shadows in the Shade will feature Johnny Marr on Rivers of Rivers and posthumous contributions from Jeremiah Green.
